title: Healthy No Bake Brownie Batter Bars (4 Ingredients)
description: These 4 ingredient no bake brownie batter bars broke the internet. They are healthy, rich, fudgy, anti-inflammatory and come together in 10 minutes of prep time.

hero.alt: Hand holding no-bake dark chocolate brownie bars with glossy topping and sea salt flakes

thumbnail.alt: Healthy no-bake brownie batter bars recipe card - 4 ingredient vegan dessert

instructions.text: Add all of the ingredients apart from the dark chocolate to a food processor and blend until combined.
Line a small container and transfer the batter. Press the batter down firmly.
Melt the dark chocolate and spread on top of the pressed batter.
Place in the freezer for 20 minutes or until the chocolate is set.
Remove from freezer, sprinkle with sea salt if desired, slice and enjoy!

notes: This is a small batch recipe. Feel free to double it for more servings.
Use a hot knife to slice cleanly if cutting straight from the freezer.
Let the bars sit at room temperature for a few minutes before eating for the best texture.

story.subtitle: rich, decadent and ovenless
paragraphs: these no bake 4 ingredient brownie batter bars were one of my first recipes to ever go viral! and to this day i still get remake pics of these bars in ur kitchen and nothing warms my heart more <3. these are perfect for when you're craving a sweet treat but absolutely do not want to turn the oven on. they're decadent, rich, chocolatey, and taste like brownie batter but you only need four ingredients, a food processor, and about 10 minutes of your time.

i created these one night when i wanted a decadent chocolatey dessert after dinner but with minimal ingredients and minimal time. once i figured out that almond flour and cacao and maple syrup mixed together tastes wildly better and richer than you'd ever think it would, i couldn't stop making them. i've been making some version of this recipe for years and i love using it as a base in other recipes too like my viral no bake blueberry chocolate bars. it really is a staple recipe in my household!

the brownie batter is mainly made from almond flour, which is naturally rich in healthy fats, plant-based protein, and vitamin E. it gives the bars a satisfying density that makes them so filling for a dessert of this size. combined with the cacao powder, you get a healthy dose of magnesium and antioxidants, particularly polyphenols, which are compounds associated with supporting cardiovascular health and reducing inflammation. these brownie batter bars taste very indulgent but they pack a punch nutritionally too! calorie wise they will be denser due to the almond flour but you can reduce the serving size if needed, this also means that they are more satiating than other flours and less feels like more which is why the recipe is intentionally small batch.

the sweetness in these no bake brownie batter bars comes from maple syrup but dates work just as well! many readers have made this recipe with dates instead and some have said they even prefer it taste-wise to the maple syrup! so you can use your preference here and opt for either. since this is a no bake recipe, you can taste the batter as you go and add in more dates or maple syrup as needed. texture wise, it doesn't actually need to come together in a ball. it may still look crumbly but you should be able to shape the dough in your hands or when pressed with a spoon or spatula. start with around 5 to 7 soft medjool dates depending on their size and stickiness, and blend until a sticky paste forms before combining with the other ingredients.

i love this recipe because it truly is so forgiving and you can't really mess it up. if it's not coming together add a little more maple syrup or dates and if it's too wet add a touch more cacao powder or almond flour. although this recipe is pretty much foolproof it never hurts to do a lil troubleshooting beforehand: 1) use a high power food processor instead of a blender. this recipe has a higher ratio of dry ingredients to wet because the speed of the food processor releases the natural oils in the almond flour which helps the batter come together. a blender normally doesn't have the same power and results in crumblier bars. 2) opt for fresh fine almond flour instead of coarse almond flour for the best results and texture.

more on the texture: it is very fudgy and chewy, almost like the inside of an underbaked brownie which is exactly the goal for a brownie batter recipe. to get the bars to slice cleanly rather than crumble, press the mixture firmly into your container and make sure it's gone into the freezer for at least 20 minutes before you try to cut it. i use the back of a spoon and then a spatula to press it down as tightly as possible and to make sure it's level. then i drizzle the melted dark chocolate and coconut oil mixture and spread. once set it becomes a glossy double chocolate layer with a satisfying crunch. the contrast between the set chocolate topping and the soft and chewy brownie batter dough is perfection. finally, top with a sprinkle of sea salt which is non-negotiable. it breaks the sweetness perfectly and complements the rich cacao flavour, so don't skip it pretty pls!

these are a great recipe to keep in your freezer for whenever a chocolate craving strikes. they store brilliantly and taste amazing straight from the freezer. for another no bake chocolate treat, try my mango yogurt bites or hot chocolate fudge cups next.

tips: This is a small batch recipe. Double all ingredients if you want a larger serving or are making these for sharing.
Use a hot knife to slice the bars cleanly if cutting straight from the freezer. Run the knife under hot water, dry it, then slice.
Let the bars sit out at room temperature for a few minutes before eating for a softer, fudgier texture. Straight from the freezer they are firmer and more snappy.
Add a teaspoon of coconut oil to the melted dark chocolate for a shinier, glossier topping that sets with a beautiful finish.

faq.question: How should I store these no bake brownie batter bars?
faq.answer: Store them in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days. For longer storage, keep them in the freezer in a freezer-safe container and let them thaw for 5 to 10 minutes before serving. They taste great cold from the fridge or just barely thawed from the freezer.

faq.question: Can I substitute the maple syrup?
faq.answer: Date syrup is another great option and adds a deeper, more caramel-like sweetness. Many readers have also used blended dates instead of liquid sweetener with great success. Start with around 5 to 7 Medjool dates depending on their size and stickiness, and blend until a sticky paste forms before combining with the other ingredients.

faq.question: Can I freeze brownie batter bars?
faq.answer: Yes, these freeze really well and are honestly one of my favourite treats eaten straight from the freezer. Once the chocolate topping has set, slice them into bars and store in a freezer-safe airtight container. They keep for up to 2 months and can be enjoyed straight from the freezer for a firmer texture or thawed slightly for something softer.

faq.question: Are these brownie batter bars gluten-free?
faq.answer: Yes, they're naturally gluten-free since they're made with almond flour instead of traditional wheat flour. There is no gluten-containing ingredient in this recipe. If you are particularly sensitive, ensure your cacao powder and dark chocolate are certified gluten-free as cross-contamination can occasionally occur during processing.

faq.question: Are these refined sugar-free?
faq.answer: These bars are sweetened with maple syrup, which is a natural, unrefined sweetener. Always check your dark chocolate label if you need the bars to be fully refined sugar-free, as not all dark chocolates are made without refined sugar. Brands that use coconut sugar or no added sweetener work best for a fully refined sugar-free version.

faq.question: How do I make the chocolate topping shiny and glossy?
faq.answer: Add a teaspoon of coconut oil to the warm melted chocolate and stir until fully combined before spreading on top of the bars. The coconut oil thins the chocolate slightly and creates a beautiful glossy finish that sets with a nice snap.

faq.question: Can I add mix-ins to these brownie batter bars?
faq.answer: Absolutely. Stir in a small handful of chopped nuts, cacao nibs, or a tablespoon of nut butter into the brownie base before pressing it into the container. You can also add a swirl of peanut butter or almond butter on top of the melted chocolate before it sets for a nutty twist. Sprinkle with flaky sea salt after slicing for a flavour contrast that works really well.

faq.question: Can I use a blender instead of a food processor?
faq.answer: It is not recommended to use a blender instead of a food processor. Blenders are not as powerful and, since this recipe has only one liquid to bind the dry ingredients, it relies heavily on the high speed of a food processor to release the natural oils in the almond flour, which act as an additional binder.

faq.question: Why are my bars crumbly?
faq.answer: If your brownie batter bars aren't coming together, it could be due to a few reasons. First, make sure you're using fine almond flour rather than coarse, as this allows the natural oils to release more effectively. The freshness of your almond flour will also play a big role. To fix this, you can add more maple syrup until the bars bind, or if the dough is already sweet enough, mix in a tablespoon or so of your favourite nut or seed butter. Make sure you're using a high-powered food processor and not a blender. It's also worth noting that the dough is not meant to come together into a ball. It will still look a little crumbly, but you should be able to mould it in your hands and have it stick together.

alternatives: Cocoa powder (works just as well for rich chocolate flavour)
Omit for a simpler bar with just the brownie base
